source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Excessive span can contribute to manager overload and reduce support available to staff and care teams","B":"Span of control affects payroll only and has no documented relationship to managers or staff outcomes","C":"The largest possible span always improves supervision because one manager can standardize every decision","D":"Patient acuity, unit complexity, and staff experience should be ignored when deciding managerial workload"}}
source_row.rationale: Research on nurse-manager span of control shows that it is multidimensional and that excessively expanded spans can contribute to manager overload or burnout and lower staff or patient satisfaction. Staffing, complexity, acuity, and manager factors matter.
source_row.source_detail: 2023 concept analysis, PMID 37159015; consequences of expanded span and multidimensional determinants; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: Journal of Healthcare Management — Impact of Span of Control on Nurse Managers and Hospital Outcomes
source_row.stem: Why should a health system avoid setting a nurse manager's span of control solely by maximizing the number of direct reports?
